h1:
Things to Do in Chumphon
Worth a Trip at Least Once
intro: Chumphon is the gateway to the south that plenty of people just drive through on their way to Koh Tao or Koh Samui, without realizing the province itself has clear water, long quiet beaches, and snorkeling islands that still feel under-the-radar. You can do sea, islands, mountains, and town all in one trip. We picked the spots that real visitors say are worth it, mixing sea, islands, town, and culture, with opening hours and rough prices so planning is easier.

blocks.html: Chumphon's attractions are strung along more than 200 km of coastline, roughly split into three zones. The south, around Mueang district, is home to Sai Ree Beach and the Krom Luang Chumphon shrine, the starting point for sea trips and the pier for island snorkeling. The north is Pathio district, with Thung Wua Laen Beach, Arunothai Beach, Khao Din So, and seaside cafes. The smart way to plan is to base yourself in one zone and explore from there, rather than driving north to south every day, since the distances add up.

blocks.text: Top Chumphon attractions (ordered by how often people mention them)

blocks.html: The list below isn't a ranking of which place is better than another. It's ordered by how often first-time visitors to Chumphon make the stop. Pick and choose to build your own days. Most are free or charge a small entry fee, except the snorkeling trips, which are boat packages.

items.name: Sai Ree Beach
items.blurb: A long white-sand beach with clear water framed by mountains, this is Chumphon town's main beach. Easy to stroll, swim, kayak, or grab a seat at a seafood spot right on the sand. It's also the launch point for sea trips and the pier out to the snorkeling islands.
items.meta: Sai Ree subdistrict, Mueang · ~20 km from town, about 30 min by car
items.price: Free beach access · food/drinks priced per venue

items.name: Krom Luang Chumphon Khet Udomsak Shrine (Sai Ree Beach)
items.blurb: A memorial to Prince Abhakara, revered as the father of the Royal Thai Navy, set on a rise at the north end of Sai Ree Beach. There's a replica warship and a wide sea-view point. People come to pay respects and ask for blessings around work and travel.

items.name: Chumphon Island Snorkeling (Ngam Noi, Ngam Yai, Ran Pet, Ran Kai)
items.blurb: The highlight of Chumphon's sea is snorkeling over healthy sea-anemone gardens and coral. Koh Ran Pet is known for its big anemone fields, while Ngam Noi and Ngam Yai have clear water and plenty of fish. Some trips also stop for crab at Koh Yor. Boats leave from Sai Ree pier or Pak Nam.
items.meta: Boats from Sai Ree Beach / Pak Nam · morning out, afternoon back
items.price: Chartered boat tour ~1,000–1,500 THB/person, depending on package and group size

items.name: Thung Wua Laen Beach (Pathio)
items.blurb: A long, shallow, fine-sand beach in Pathio district. The gentle waves make it good for family swimming, and there are resorts and seafood restaurants along the sand for a long, relaxed sit. It's the most popular base on the northern side.
items.meta: Saphli subdistrict, Pathio · ~30–40 min by car from town
items.price: Free beach access · food/lodging priced per venue

items.name: Khao Din So (Viewpoint and Raptor Migration Spot)
items.blurb: A peak in Pathio district with a viewpoint over the bay and open sea. It's an internationally known raptor-migration watching site, and from September to November tens of thousands of birds pass overhead. Parts of the road up are steep and the facilities are run down, so come prepared and check the road condition before you go.
items.meta: Bang Son subdistrict, Pathio · open roughly 06:00–18:00

items.name: Pathio Tree Tunnel (Baan Ton Mai Uat Chum)
items.blurb: A seaside cafe and restaurant in Pathio built around big old trees, with a tree-tunnel corner and sea views for photos. It's a nice stop for coffee and the view between spots on the northern side, and people tend to come from late morning to evening.
items.meta: Pathio district · open roughly 09:00–18:00 (check the closing day first)
items.price: Coffee/food per menu, starting in the low hundreds THB

items.name: Arunothai Beach
items.blurb: A long, quiet beach on the Pathio side. The name means 'dawn,' fitting since it's a lovely seaside sunrise spot. Few people, calm atmosphere, perfect for an early-morning walk in the breeze before your trip starts.
items.meta: Pathio district · near Thung Wua Laen Beach

items.name: Pak Nam Chumphon
items.blurb: A river-mouth district by the sea that's a fishing community and harbor. There's a fresh seafood market, waterfront seafood restaurants, and the ferry pier out to Koh Tao and Koh Phangan. A great place for dinner and watching the fishing life.
items.meta: Pak Nam subdistrict, Mueang · ~15 min by car from town
items.price: Free to wander · seafood priced per venue

items.name: Mu Ko Chumphon National Park (Nature Study Center)
items.blurb: A nature study center on the Sai Ree Beach side, with a wooden boardwalk through the mangrove forest. Shady and pleasant, it shows off the river-mouth ecosystem and is good for an easy walk and bringing kids to learn about nature.
items.meta: Sai Ree subdistrict, Mueang · open during office hours
items.price: Foreigner entry per national-park rate · Thais usually free or a small fee

items.name: Wat Khao Chedi (Pathio)
items.blurb: A hilltop temple in Pathio district. Walk up to the chedi terrace and you get a 360-degree view of the sea and town. It's a sunrise and merit-making spot that locals recommend. There are stairs to climb, so save a little energy.
items.meta: Bang Son subdistrict, Pathio · go up early on a clear morning for the best view
items.price: No entry fee · donate as you wish

items.name: Saphli Beach
items.blurb: A curved beach belonging to the Pathio fishing community, with a shrine and brightly colored fishing boats lined up for photos. The water is clear enough to swim, and the homey, uncrowded vibe makes it an easy add-on from Thung Wua Laen.
items.meta: Saphli subdistrict, Pathio · near Thung Wua Laen Beach

items.name: Chumphon Town Markets and Old Quarter
items.blurb: The center of Chumphon town has a morning market, a night market, and robusta-coffee shops the province is known for. You can walk and eat southern food, khanom jeen, and seafood, then buy roasted coffee to take home. Good for a day off from the sea.
items.meta: Mueang Chumphon district · morning market opens early, night market opens in the evening
items.price: Free to wander · street food from a few tens of THB

blocks.title: Planning tips
blocks.html: Island snorkeling trips depend heavily on the wind and waves. The good window is February to May, when the water is clear and the sea is calm. Late in the year the monsoon can keep boats in port. Book a tour that checks the weather for you and ask about their reschedule/refund terms first. If you're coming to watch raptors at Khao Din So, October is the peak of the migration.

blocks.text: For the sea, beaches, and snorkeling

blocks.html: The heart of Chumphon is the sea, with beaches that are longer and quieter than Hua Hin or Samui, and snorkeling islands that still feel under-the-radar. There's everything from a chill beach sit to a full-day boat trip. If you love clear water and coral, set aside a day for a snorkeling boat.

items.name: Sai Ree Beach
items.blurb: The town's main beach: white sand, clear water, the Krom Luang Chumphon shrine, and seafood right on the sand. The base for sea trips on the southern side.

items.name: Chumphon Islands
items.blurb: Snorkel over anemone gardens and coral at Ran Pet, Ran Kai, Ngam Noi, and Ngam Yai. Boat out in the morning, back in the afternoon.

items.name: Thung Wua Laen–Saphli
items.blurb: Long beaches with gentle waves on the Pathio side, good for families, with resorts and seaside restaurants for a long sit.

items.name: Arunothai Beach
items.blurb: A quiet beach and seaside sunrise spot with few people, good for an early walk in the breeze.

blocks.html: Chumphon isn't only about the sea. The Pathio side has Khao Din So and Wat Khao Chedi, both with wide sea views from the top, while the Krom Luang Chumphon shrine is a spiritual anchor for the whole province. Dress modestly when entering the shrine and temple grounds.

items: Krom Luang Chumphon Shrine — a memorial to Prince Abhakara by Sai Ree Beach with wide sea views, popular for blessings around work.
Khao Din So — an internationally known viewpoint and raptor-migration spot, peaking in October.
Wat Khao Chedi (Pathio) — a hilltop chedi terrace with 360-degree views and a sunrise spot.
Mu Ko Chumphon Nature Study Center — a shady mangrove boardwalk, good for kids.

blocks.html: The other side of Chumphon is easygoing town life. Chumphon is one of Thailand's big robusta-coffee growing areas, so the town has cafes using genuinely local beans. The morning market has southern food and khanom jeen to try, while Pak Nam Chumphon is where you eat fresh waterfront seafood. Good for a day off from the sea.

items: Pak Nam Chumphon — a fresh seafood market and waterfront seafood restaurants, near the pier to Koh Tao.
Chumphon Morning Market — southern food, khanom jeen, and fresh ingredients, good for breakfast on foot.
Robusta coffee cafes — in-town shops roasting Chumphon beans, good to buy as a gift.
Night market — budget-friendly dinner eats, open from evening to late.

blocks.html: Here's a sample three-day, two-night plan that alternates a southern-side beach day, a snorkeling day, and a northern Pathio day. Adjust the timing to reality. Having your own car or a rental makes things far easier, since the attractions are spread out and public transport is inconvenient.

blocks.label: Day 1
blocks.title: Sai Ree Beach + Krom Luang Shrine + Pak Nam

items.activity: Arrive in Chumphon town, breakfast at the morning market or khanom jeen
Head to Sai Ree Beach, swim and stroll along the sand
items.note: Before noon the sun isn't too harsh

items.activity: Seafood lunch on Sai Ree Beach
Pay respects at the Krom Luang Chumphon shrine, see the replica warship and sea views
Head to Pak Nam Chumphon for the fishing life and a waterfront seafood dinner
Board the boat at Sai Ree / Pak Nam pier and head to the islands
items.note: Check the weather with the tour before your travel day

items.activity: Snorkel at Koh Ran Pet, see the anemone gardens
On to Ngam Noi / Ngam Yai, clear water with lots of fish
Lunch on the boat / stop for crab at Koh Yor
Back to shore, rest, and an easy dinner in town

blocks.label: Day 3
blocks.title: Northern Pathio side — Thung Wua Laen, Khao Din So, cafe

items.activity: Early wake-up for sunrise at Arunothai Beach or Wat Khao Chedi
items.note: Skip it if you don't want the early start

items.activity: Swim at Thung Wua Laen Beach, stop at Saphli Beach for fishing-boat photos
Head up Khao Din So for views of the bay and sea
items.note: Some sections are steep, check the road condition first

items.activity: Sit at the Pathio tree-tunnel cafe, coffee with a view before heading back

blocks.title: Getting around Chumphon
blocks.html: In town there are songthaews and motorcycle taxis, but attractions like Sai Ree, Pathio, and Khao Din So are far apart with little public transport. We'd suggest renting a car or motorbike in town. For island trips, book the boat tour ahead, since there are no scheduled boats.

faq.q: What are the must-do attractions in Chumphon?
faq.a: What first-time visitors usually don't skip is Sai Ree Beach and the Krom Luang Chumphon shrine on the town side, the Chumphon island snorkeling trip (Ran Pet, Ran Kai, Ngam Noi, Ngam Yai) for the sea, Thung Wua Laen Beach and Khao Din So on the Pathio side, and Pak Nam Chumphon for seafood. You can mix sea, islands, town, and culture.

faq.q: How many days do you need in Chumphon?
faq.a: Two to three days is about right for a first visit, giving you a beach day on the town side, one day of island snorkeling, and another day on the Pathio side. If you have more time, continue on to Koh Tao or down to Surat Thani, since Chumphon is a convenient connection point.

faq.q: When is the best time to snorkel in Chumphon?
faq.a: The clear-water, calm-sea window is February to May, the best time to take an island snorkeling boat. Late in the year is monsoon season on the Gulf side, with rough seas and some days when boats can't go out. Book a tour that checks the weather for you and ask about reschedule terms first.

faq.q: When should you go to Khao Din So to see raptors?
faq.a: The raptor migration season runs roughly September to November, peaking around mid to late October, when you'll see large flocks passing overhead. Clear mornings are best. That said, the facilities on the hill are run down, so come prepared and check the road condition before heading up.

faq.q: Can you visit Chumphon without your own car?
faq.a: You can get around town with songthaews and motorcycle taxis, but Sai Ree Beach, Pathio, and Khao Din So are far apart with little public transport. We'd suggest renting a car or motorbike. For island trips, book the boat tour ahead.
